title: Other oil products: hardcoded pass-through 1 and margin 0
why: Row 759 holds typed constants: raw price-control coefficient M759 = 1 and margin O759 = 0, while every other oil product (rows 755-758) reads both from the IMF price dataset.
ref: M758 and O758 (kerosene), the same formulas with $G758. IFERROR keeps the old constant if the dataset has no oop entry.
effect: Egypt: pass-through 0 and margin about 7.95 $/bbl from the dataset (as the prototype). The other-oil-products retail price no longer falls with the oil price to the floor, and the tenfold rise in their fuel use by 2030 goes away.

title: Population growth path
where: Mitigation row 428 (feeds 429, 481, 2428, 6196 and the policy block)
why: From 2026 the population row carries 2% a year, then 3% (2030) and 4% (2031 on, by repeating the last growth): Egypt 185.2 million in 2041. The legacy sheet UNPop (UN WPP 2024) gives 147.0 million.
ref: Sheet UNPop, row egy.lp (UN World Population Prospects 2024), already in legacy. Growth is chained on the 2025 WEO level so there is no break in 2026.
effect: Egypt population 2040: 178.1 to 132.4 million; 2041: 185.2 to 134.0 million. Rows 429, 481 and 2428 follow automatically, so agriculture, waste and per-capita GDP drivers fall after 2026.

title: GDP effect added to GDP growth every year
why: Post-policy growth = g + e (row 2446 = SUM(2444:2445)), so a steady GDP level effect e adds e to growth every year and compounds; row 2443 then chains on the pre-policy level.
ref: Row 2445 is already the level effect lagged one year (= previous year of row 8274); the fix uses it as a level, as the label of 2443 ("GDP post-policy") says.
effect: No change on the NoPropData file (row 8288 is stripped to 0). With a steady effect of 0.5%, GDP is +0.5% instead of about +10% after 20 years.

title: ETS quick estimate linear in the semi-elasticity
why: The quick price estimate divides the reduction by the semi-elasticity. In the NoPropData file L1868:AE1868 hold stored zeros (formula stripped); in a full file they hold the linear quotient.

title: Waste abated with the livestock curve
why: Waste reduction = M6168 (livestock share) although the waste curve inputs (rows 6186-6190) are computed.
ref: Rows 6168 (livestock) and 6180 (rice): = MAX(0, MIN(1, $L curve x fee ^ $M curve)).
effect: None in the baseline (no methane fee). With a fee, waste CH4 follows its own abatement curve.

title: Navigation missing from the local pollutant totals
why: Each pollutant block has transport rows rod gso/die/lpg/ker/nga, ral die and avi jfu, but no navigation row, so navigation never enters the transport, "Other" or total rows. This cannot be fixed by editing an existing cell.
ref: The "ral die" row of the same block (e.g. 6808 for SO2) for the formula; navigation fuel use is rows 5508-5515.
effect: Adds navigation emissions (Egypt navigation: about 291 ktoe of other oil products in 2022).
note: Steps, in the 8 pollutant blocks (PM2.5 6590, NOx 6692, SO2 6794, VOC 6896, BC 6998, OC 7100, CH4 7202, CO 7309) of the baseline and of the policy block (+6,316): (1) select the "avi jfu" row (6605, 6707, 6809, 6911, 7013, 7115, 7218, 7324) and insert one row above it, so the transport SUM ranges and the totals expand by themselves; (2) in the new row type B = "nav", C = "oop" and copy the year formula of the "ral die" row directly above; (3) add the new cell to the "Other" (oth) air-pollution row of the block (6686, 6788, 6890, 6992, 7094, 7196, 7405; CH4: no such row). Do all baseline blocks first, then the policy blocks, and check that BaselineFirstRow/PolicyScenarioFirstRow moved with them. In the NoPropData file every emission row holds 0 (GAINS factors stripped), so check the copied formula in the full file.

title: Domestic aviation: GDP growth and shock swapped
why: Aviation rows raise the shock (1+M2439) to eps_Y x income factor and multiply by (1+M2446) with elasticity 1; coal and gas multiply by (1+M2439) a second time; jet fuel uses the diesel income elasticity _el_inc_die_rod.
ref: Standard row 5399 (road diesel): L x (1+M2446)^(eps_Y x M2433) x (1+M2439) x price terms. Jet fuel takes the oil income elasticity, as its other elasticities (_el_dem_oil_rod, _el_eff_oil_rod) already do.
effect: Egypt jet fuel (707 ktoe in 2022): the 2023-2024 shock now enters in full (-20.8%, +9.2%) and GDP growth with eps_Y x income factor; the repo survey (Sector_Equations_Survey) puts the standard form at x0.90 (2023), x0.82 (2030) and x0.68 (2040) of legacy. Other aviation fuels are 0 for Egypt.

title: Pass-through applied twice in the first projected year
where: Mitigation floating subsidy/tax rows (code cs), 12 fuel blocks
why: The base value $J (= the 2024 value) already carries (1 - pass-through) from the history formula (columns K:N); the projection multiplies (2024 price - price + $J) by (1 - pass-through) again, so the floating subsidy jumps in the first projected year when pass-through is between 0 and 1.
ref: History formula of the same rows (K:N): (excise - other parts) x (1 - $J pass-through), applied once.
effect: None for Egypt (bucketed pass-through 0 or 1). With pass-through 0.5 or 0.8 (Manual price controls, other countries), no jump in 2025.

title: Balance of payments: oil without the share traded
why: The value of the change in oil net imports is change in use x price, while gas (row 18172, x $H741) and coal (row 18178, x $H743) multiply by the share traded of the trade-balance table (rows 741-743). Oil products have a share of 0.47 (H742), so the oil effect is about twice too large.
ref: Rows 18172 (gas) and 18178 (coal) of the same section; H742 = share traded of oil products.
effect: Reported balance of payments only: the oil line falls to 47% (Egypt 2028: -1.75 to -0.83 bn USD); rows 18200, 18203, 18207, 18218 follow.

title: Residential leakage to biomass inconsistent
why: (a) The not-exempt rows subtract the (negative) fossil change, so they rise, and the totals add the changes back cumulatively: fossil use is not reduced. (b) Kerosene uses the LPG price base (L5546 in 5587) and the LPG share (M5582 in 5588), and has two "Change in kerosene" rows. (c) The fossil change is multiplied by the fossil efficiency and the biomass gain by the biomass efficiency again, so energy is not conserved.
ref: Labels of the block: "Change in X" is a change in fuel; "Equivalent Biomass" (rows 5578, 5584, 5591, already = change x fossil efficiency / biomass efficiency) is the biomass that replaces it. Biomass total 5560 keeps its cumulative SUM; the fossil rows carry the reduction forward themselves.
effect: None while BiomassLeakage = No (E1785 = 0, Egypt). With leakage on, fossil cooking fuel falls and biomass rises by the same useful energy.

title: Road other biofuels: wrong price and terms
why: Row 5406 uses the bioethanol price (5390) because the other-biofuels price row 5392 is empty, puts the shadow price through eps_U, has an efficiency term (M5390/M5390)^eps_F that is always 1, and uses $M2259 (coal exemption phase-out) as additional efficiency.
ref: Row 5389 (road biomass price: = (M2720)+M2721*M2271) for the price; standard row 5399 for the form, with the biomass shadow price row 2388 and road additional efficiency $M2199. The elasticity names are those legacy already uses in 5406.
effect: None for Egypt (no road other biofuels).

title: Self-generated renewables in aviation and navigation take the shock from wrong rows
why: Row 5491 multiplies by (1+M2512) (coal industry new excise) and row 5516 by (1+M2473) (blank row) instead of the shock row 2439. Row 5491 also has the aviation swap of L42.
ref: Row 5407 (road self-generated renewables).
effect: None for Egypt (no self-generated renewables in these sectors).

title: Residential initially-exempt rows: no income factor; starred "Yes*" exemption test
why: The exemption split itself works: L5564:L5566 = IFNA(IF($L$1784=B,(1-$K$1795)*base, base), base) and L5568:L5570 = IFNA(IF($L$1784=B, $K$1795*base, 0), 0) (text read from the .xlsb; the LibreOffice conversion had shown IFNA(0)). It is 0 in the Egypt run only because I1784 = 0 (ExemptMostCook off). Two defects remain: the initially-exempt rows M5568:M5570 grow with (1+g)^eps_Y without the income factor M2433 (the not-exempt rows 5564-5566 have it), and the AlwaysExemptResLPGKer test in rows 5546-5547 compares with "Yes" while the input list uses "Yes*"/"No*".
ref: The exempt share is legacy's own row 1795 ("Exempted ... proportion", most-used cooking fuel L1784). Income factor as in the not-exempt rows 5564-5566.
effect: None in the default Egypt run (ExemptMostCook off; AlwaysExemptResLPGKer No). With ExemptMostCook on, the initially-exempt share grows like the rest; with "Yes*" the exemption applies.
note: Redone from the .xlsb (2026-10-19): the earlier start-row edits of L5564:L5570 were built on converted text and are dropped (the split already exists). M5568:M5570 are also edited by L94 (exponent): apply both substitutions.
